Stroke and Aneurysm
Deﬁ nition
A stroke (cerebrovascular accident) occurs when a sudden 
interruption of blood ﬂ ow to the brain deprives neurons and
other brain cells of nutrients and oxygen and thereby alters 
brain function.34 When blood vessels supplying blood to the 
brain are obstructed, as with a clot, the stroke is classiﬁ ed as an 
ischemic stroke. Ischemic strokes are the most common form,
accounting for about 80% of all strokes. Transient ischemic 
attacks (TIAs) or “mini-strokes” are deﬁ ned as an episode of 
ischemia where blood ﬂ ow is quickly restored and symptoms
resolve within 24 hours. A hemorrhagic stroke occurs when a
blood vessel in the brain ruptures. Th is is most likely to occur
when blood vessel walls are weakened by hypertension or other
conditions, including aneurysms. An aneurysm is deﬁ ned as
